description: Prefer fd over find and rg over grep -r when they are installed, with a cheat sheet shown once per session.

find-fd.message:
find and grep -r are blocked in favour of fd and rg: much faster, and they respect .gitignore. fd cannot express some find predicates (-perm, -newer REF, -atime/-ctime, -printf beyond paths, -inum, -samefile, -links, -ok, OR across different predicate kinds); for those the original command is fine.

── fd/rg cheat sheet (`{which:fd|fdfind} -h` / `rg -h` print the short help) ──
TRAPS — read first:
  Both skip .gitignore'd paths AND dot-files/dirs by default; find/grep don't.
    Want everything?  {which:fd|fdfind} -u (= -H -I)    rg -uu (= --no-ignore --hidden; -uuu adds --binary, but only -a prints binary matches)
  {which:fd|fdfind} takes a REGEX on the basename: `{which:fd|fdfind} *.py` is a shell-glob trap → {which:fd|fdfind} -e py or {which:fd|fdfind} -g '*.py';  -p matches the full path
  rg's first non-flag arg is the PATTERN: `rg src/` searches for the text "src/" (exit 0, no warning) → rg PAT src/
  rg silently skips binary files (grep prints "Binary file matches"); -a searches them as text
  Under sudo, brew binaries are not on secure_path:  sudo "$(command -v {which:fd|fdfind})" …

{which:fd|fdfind} [flags] [regex] [path…]   smart-case; -g glob, -F literal, --exact whole name; `{which:fd|fdfind} -- '-x'` for patterns starting with -
  find . -name '*.py'              →  {which:fd|fdfind} -e py            (or {which:fd|fdfind} -g '*.py')
  find . -iname '*foo*'            →  {which:fd|fdfind} foo              (find . -name foo, exact → {which:fd|fdfind} --exact foo)
  find . -type f|d|l               →  {which:fd|fdfind} -t f | -t d | -t l    (-t x executables, -t e empty)
  find . -maxdepth 2 / -mindepth 1 →  {which:fd|fdfind} -d 2 / --min-depth 1   (--exact-depth N)
  find . -path '*/node_modules' -prune -o …  →  {which:fd|fdfind} -E node_modules   (glob, repeatable)
  find . -mtime -1 / -mmin -30     →  {which:fd|fdfind} --changed-within 1d / 30min    (--changed-before 2weeks; mtime only)
  find . -size +10M                →  {which:fd|fdfind} -S +10mi         (find's M is MiB = mi; m = MB; unit required: b k m g t ki mi gi ti)
  find . -user core                →  {which:fd|fdfind} --owner core     (--owner :group, '!user' negates)
  find . -exec cmd {} \;           →  {which:fd|fdfind} … -x cmd {}     ({/} name, {//} dir, {.} no ext; -x last; PARALLEL, no shell; -j1 = sequential)
  find . -exec cmd {} + / -delete  →  {which:fd|fdfind} … -X cmd / -X rm
  find . -xdev                     →  {which:fd|fdfind} --one-file-system;   -L follows symlinks;   -0 for xargs -0;   -a absolute paths
  no extension: {which:fd|fdfind} '^[^.]+$' -t f;   OR by regex: {which:fd|fdfind} '\.(py|js)$';   {which:fd|fdfind} PAT --and PAT2;   --format '{//}' prints path fields only

rg [flags] PATTERN [path…]       case-sensitive by default; line numbers + per-file headings automatic; -w -x -F -v -o -A -B -C as in grep
  grep -rn foo .                   →  rg foo              (-N no line numbers, -H/-I force/suppress filenames)
  grep -ri foo                     →  rg -i foo           (-S smart-case, -s force sensitive)
  grep -r --include='*.py' foo     →  rg -t py foo   or   rg -g '*.py' foo      (rg --type-list; -g beats -t)
  grep -r --exclude-dir=vendor     →  rg -g '!vendor' foo       (include-globs for dirs need /**: -g 'src/**'; later globs win; -T py = not type)
  grep -rl / -rL / -rc             →  rg -l / --files-without-match / -c    (-c omits 0-count files: --include-zero; --count-matches = per match)
  grep -rE … / -rP …               →  rg …  / rg -P …     (-P for look-around and backreferences);  `rg -e -foo` for patterns starting with -
  grep -ro foo                     →  rg -o foo           (-r REPL rewrites output only, never files)
  grep -rz … / multi-line          →  rg -z … (decompressor must be on PATH; silent if missing) / rg -U 'a\nb' (`.` needs --multiline-dotall to cross lines)
  find . -type f | …               →  rg --files [path]   (candidate files under the same ignore rules; a real search additionally skips binaries)
  -m N max per file, --max-filesize 5M, --sort path for stable order

Combine: rg walks the tree itself, so `find … | xargs grep` is usually just `rg PAT [path]`.
  Filters rg lacks (size, mtime, owner, depth, file type) → {which:fd|fdfind} … -X rg -n PAT   or   {which:fd|fdfind} -0 … | xargs -0 rg PAT
find-fd.messageShort:
find and grep -r are blocked in favour of fd and rg: much faster, and they respect .gitignore. fd cannot express some find predicates (-perm, -newer REF, -atime/-ctime, -printf beyond paths, -inum, -samefile, -links, -ok, OR across different predicate kinds); for those the original command is fine.

{which:fd|fdfind} [regex | -g GLOB] [path]   (-e ext, -t f|d, -d depth, -E exclude, -u = ignored+hidden)
   pattern is a REGEX on the basename — `{which:fd|fdfind} *.py` is a shell trap, use -e py; -p to match the path
rg PATTERN [path]              (-t py / -g '*.py', -l, -i, -w, -F, -C3, -uu = ignored+hidden)
   first arg is the PATTERN — `rg src/` searches for the text "src/"; pass the dir as the 2nd arg
(The full cheat sheet was shown earlier in this session; `{which:fd|fdfind} -h` / `rg -h` print the short help.)
